P1.evidence: The rep acknowledged having setter notes but did not read any of them back to make the prospect feel seen — 'I've already got quite a bit of information, right? But I just want to hear it from you.' He did use Derek's notes later ('I think Derek mentioned to me that you have never had that before, right?'), which is why this scores partial rather than a miss. The frame carried two of four parts plus the disqualification promise: 'go over where you're currently at, where you want to go, see if we can help you bridge that gap. If we can, take you through it. If not, I'll point you in the right direction, okay?' Agreement was sought and given. The open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in the batch on the checks that were run. Age, height and weight all asked in one pass ('you're saying you're 100 kgs, I think you're 5'6", right? how old are you actually?'). The injury question is the standout — 'when it comes to overall your mobility at the moment as well... are those things at the moment?' — which produced an unusually complete history with mechanisms and durations: the 2018 AC separation, the ice-skating re-injury, six to eight years of intermittent shoulder trouble, the elbow, the doctor-diagnosed distal hamstring dysfunction eighteen months ago, and the sciatic tenderness. Training week and lack of progress were covered exhaustively, and nutrition was probed well beyond the headline, including a specific and productive question about sauces and processed food. Against that: occupation was never asked and arrived only when the prospect volunteered 'I work in IT as a cyber security engineer' at 00:26:14 — the ICP-deciding fact, twenty-six minutes in, by luck. Health conditions were never asked as distinct from injuries. Sleep was never asked at all, in a fifty-three minute call. Energy was reached only through the goal framing.

P3.evidence: The 1-to-10 scale opened it and the follow-up did the real work: 'What would that 10 of 10 Sam look like?' produced a target weight, a muscle-versus-leanness distinction, and then the prospect's own reordering of his priorities — the physique is 'the secondary thing', the real goal is 'every opportunity that comes my way, I feel ready to take it on'. The bridge ran ('what's your big why'), the future-self question ran, who-else-does-this-impact ran and reached the partner, friends, colleagues and unborn children, and the drive-through landed on turning 30, career goals and being a role model. The reflect-back was explicit and correctly subordinated the surface goal: 'the goals for you are to lose body fat to like 85 kgs, get leaner, but that's the secondary goal... the [main thing] is being free.' P3c is partial rather than a hit because the something-you-cannot-do material — the 5-10 km run with his semi-professional friend — was volunteered by the prospect rather than asked for.

P4.evidence: Effectively complete. The full attempt history came out — army selection, the regain to 110 kg, the routine-hopping across push-pull-legs and upper-lower, and the 100-300 burpees a morning that ended in shoulder and elbow damage. What happened with each was traced. The stuck question was asked ('how long do you feel like you have been sort of stuck or at least not progressing as much as you want to?') and produced a self-diagnosis the rep then confirmed: 'I get into this cycle of over-analyzing everything and changing the routine too often, and that's what I think is holding me back.' The root-cause question was asked with options offered, and the prospect named the gap in his own words: 'preventing me from overanalyzing my structure and just focus on one thing long enough to see results.' P4f is partial only because the information-isn't-the-problem line was never put as a question — the prospect got there himself: 'I like to think that I'm intelligent enough to apply things, but sometimes you just gotta admit you can't do everything on your own.'

P5.evidence: The first properly executed consequence frame in this batch, and it worked. The rep set it up explicitly — 'what we've seen with the best results of Trevor is those that have looked into the negative future' — then ran it: 'if you don't make a change, it stays going the exact same way... In a few years, you have kids running around as well. If nothing really changed, how would you look back at the last few years?' That produced the most charged material anywhere in the corpus so far: 'I would be disappointed... one of the biggest things is I don't want to end up the way I used to be.' The settle question followed directly — 'Would that be something that you would actually be willing to settle for, where nothing changes?' — and got 'No, no, no. It's not enough. We're only here for one life.' P5c is partial because the prospect volunteered the why rather than being asked for it, and P5d partial because the line in the sand came as a leading statement ('Time to make a change, right?') rather than a question.

P6.evidence: The phase that decided this call. P6a exists only as an effort question asked half an hour before the presentation — 'do you want to put an effort in... Are you willing to put the effort into fixing that?' — not a belief question about the programme. P6b was never asked, and its absence is the whole story: 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?' would have surfaced the funding wall before the price rather than after it, and the rep had already gathered enough about a decade of financial difficulty to expect it. P6c failed outright: the rep moved to the investment on the strength of 'Yeah, yeah. Sounds interesting', which is the same soft yes he acted on with Brent the day before. Fifty-three minutes of otherwise strong work went into a close that was never qualified for.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — price presented at 00:42:17 and a decision pursued across ten minutes — and no payment was collected. The prospect could not fund any structure offered, so the remaining steps were never reachable. Worth recording that the rep held the price and did not discount under sustained pressure, which is the correct behaviour and is not captured anywhere else in the phase scoring.

objection_plays.detail: The best-run money play in this batch. Isolation ran first and properly: 'Outside of the thinking about that aspect, do you feel like, yeah, I do want to do this?' — answered 'outside of kind of discussing the financial side, I would be interested.' The should-I-versus-how frame ran almost verbatim: 'is it more of a... How should I actually do this? Or is it more so, should I even do this?' — answered 'it'd be more so how.' The upfront-versus-plan move ran. Of the six financial-picture moves, cash on hand ran ('what do you feel like you would have available'), rainy-day savings ran ('do you have any set aside things at the moment... for rainy day funds?'), and monthly surplus ran and returned a hard number (£1,200). What did not run is the part that mattered: credit cards, available credit, and used-versus-available were never asked, and neither were investments. With £1,200 a month clear and a two-or-three-instalment structure on the table, credit was the obvious remaining lever and it was left untouched. The rep also disclosed the interest uplift unprompted and advised the cheaper structure.

Trigger present in substance — 'I'll have to discuss it and have a think about it' — and the rep handled the front half well. He asked what she would say, offered to bring her onto the call immediately ('If you want, you can call her in, because she's probably going to have questions. I can also answer them for her'), and then ran the isolation that resolved it: 'would it be fair to say that it just comes down to finances rather than sort of getting approval?' The prospect agreed. None of the back-half moves ran — no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger', no permission-versus-input distinction, no responsibility track, and no deposit-with-refund fallback. Defensible, because the objection genuinely resolved to money, but the play was abandoned rather than completed.

'I do have my pay review in October... I could revisit it then' is a right-time objection. The rep ran two moves well: he stress-tested the premise — 'So what if it doesn't? What if it goes the exact same way?' — and asked whether any route existed to start now. He did not run 'things never slow down', 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', or 'the only thing you can control is right now'. Instead he improvised an argument that starting now would improve the salary review itself, which the prospect declined on the merits: 'it's kind of the carrot and the stick situation, isn't it? I can't warrant that money.'

Recorded because the play was attempted against a trigger that was not there. After the prospect had disclosed almost no savings and 'my last kind of 10 years have been very complicated financially', the rep tested for a concealed fear objection: 'it sounds like it's possible financially... Could it be that you have a little bit of an uncertainty around actually taking that step for yourself?' The prospect rejected it — 'No, no, it's definitely just a financial issue' — and the rep accepted the answer and moved on, which is the right response. Noted rather than penalised, but at scale, reframing a disclosed cash constraint as psychological hesitancy is worth watching.

'I'll have to discuss it and have a think about it' contains a think-about-it as well as a spouse objection. No OA move ran. The rep went straight to isolation and money, which turned out to be the correct diagnosis, so this is a defensible miss rather than a failure — but it should be recorded as unrun rather than credited.

Script gap with a live commercial consequence. The prospect wanted the programme, could not fund $6,000 in any structure offered, and asked in effect for a way in. A lower tier exists — this same rep presented it as '$2,000 a year or $200 a month' to a different prospect the previous day — and it was never mentioned here. Instead the prospect was sent a free video. There is no scripted rule for when the lower tier is offered and when it is not, and its application across these two adjacent calls is inverted: it went to the prospect who did not want the full programme, and not to the prospect who wanted it and could not afford it.

notes: Score this as a strong process that lost anyway, which is exactly the case the spec exists to protect. Phases 2 through 5 are the best work in the batch — the injury history, the goal reordering and the consequence frame all ran properly, and the money play was close to complete. Two coachable items. First, Phase 6b: fifty-three minutes of excellent discovery went into a price presented off 'Sounds interesting', and the one question that would have exposed the funding wall was never asked. Second, credit was never explored despite £1,200 a month clear and a no-interest two-or-three-instalment option on the table. One item to escalate rather than coach: the lower tier was available and was not offered to the one prospect in this batch who needed it.
